title: Oxytocin released from mouse hypothalamus and nerve endings by extracellular applicaion of beta-NAD+ and cyclic ADP-ribose
protocol: Anaesthetise an adult male mouse with pentobarbitone sodium at a dose of 50 mg/kg.
Turn the whole brain bottom side up after cutting the optic nerve.
Isolate the hypothalamus near the optic chiasma, including the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
Place one whole hypothalamus in a 24 multi-well plate with 0.4 ml normal Locke solution on a water bath at 37°C.
Replace the incubation medium 10 times every 5 minutes.
Soak the hypothalamus tissue with a total of 6 ml of pre-warmed normal Locke solution at 37°C for 50 minutes and discard solutions.
Reserve aliquots of 0.4 ml of Locke solution after 3-minute incubation with the hypothalamus in 1.5 ml microtubes.
Change the incubation liquid to 0.4 ml of 70-mM high-potassium Locke solution.
Collect 3 min later in a microtube.
Make oxytocin standard solutions in tubes at concentrations of 1000, 500, 250, 125, 62.5, 31.25 and 15.6 pg/ml.
Pipette 100 μL of standard diluent into the NSB and B0 wells of a 96-well plate.
Pipette 100 μL of standards 1 through 7 into appropriate wells.
Pipette 100 μL of samples from 0.4 ml into appropriate wells.
Pipette 50 μL of assay buffer into the NSB wells.
Pipette 50 μL of blue conjugate into each well except TA and Blank wells.
Pipette 50 μL of yellow antibody into each well except blank, TA, and NSB wells.
Tap the plate gently to mix.
Seal the plate and incubate at 4°C for 18-24 h.
Empty the contents of the plate after incubation.
Wash each well with 400 μL of wash solution.
Repeat washing 2 more times for a total of 3 washes.
After final wash, empty wells and tap dry on a lint-free paper towel.
Add 5 μL of blue conjugate to the TA wells.
Add 200 μL of the pNpp substrate solution to each well.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour without shaking.
Add 50 μL of stop solution to each well.
Read the optical density at 405 nm with a plate reader.
Calculate oxytocin concentration from the standard curve.
Anesthetize a male mouse with pentobarbitone sodium at a dose of 50 mg/kg.
Remove the whole brain and isolate the posterior pituitary.
Incubate the posterior pituitary lobe in 1 mL of normal Locke solution for 1 minute.
Transfer to 1 mL of sucrose solution in a Teflon homogeniser.
Gently homogenize with 5-6 strokes.
Centrifuge the homogenate in a microtube for 1 min at 100 × g.
Collect the supernatant.
Centrifuge again for 4 min at 600 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resolve the pellet with 200 μL of Locke solution.
Pipette 4–5 times with a yellow tip.
Load nerve endings onto cover glasses coated with 0.1% polyornithine in a 35-mm 6-well plate.
Allow to stand for 5 min to settle.
Discard the floating nerve endings and wash the wells with 1 mL of Locke solution three times.
Replace 1 mL of Locke solution 10 times every 5 min.
Incubate the mouse hypothalamic nerve endings with 1 mL of Locke solution containing or without 100 μM 8-bromo-cADPR for 60 min.
Wash the nerve endings quickly three times with 1 mL of Locke solution.
Incubate with 1 mL of normal Locke solution containing or without 100 μM 8-bromo-cADPR.
Collect the solution incubated for 5 minutes three times every 5 minutes for basal oxytocin release.
Stimulate the preparation with 1 ml of normal Locke solution containing 100 microM beta-NAD+, cADPR, cADPcR NAAD, ADPR or 100 nM NAADP, with or without 100 microM 8-bromo-cADPR for 5 minutes.
